extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, MPEP editors, and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) involved in §101 subject-matter eligibility analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for applying and revising MPEP treatment of patent subject-matter eligibility (35 U.S.C. §101) consistent with the 2019 Revised Patent Subject Matter Eligibility Guidance, including how to apply Steps 2A and 2B, identify judicial exceptions, and formulate/support rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alice/Mayo test — Steps 2A and 2B
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise high level discussion of the 1st and 2nd steps of the test (Steps 2A and 2B in PTO guidance) and reference to Form Paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update MPEP discussion to reflect the revised approach (Step 2A prongs and Step 2B), ensure references to form paragraphs are current, and avoid language that equates 'recited' with 'directed to.' Include integration analysis in Step 2A Prong Two and ensure proper placement of 'additional elements' considerations between 2A and 2B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two Criteria For Subject Matter Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: State and apply the two criteria (prongs/steps) used to determine subject-matter eligibility for claims under §101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include instruction to 'Establish Broadest Reasonable Interpretation Of Claim As A Whole' and provide a 'Summary Of Analysis And Flowchart' for examiner use; revise wording to avoid confusing 'application' with 'practical application' (prong two).

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish Broadest Reasonable Interpretation Of Claim As A Whole
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpret the claim as a whole under the broadest reasonable interpretation when conducting the eligibility analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revise MPEP text so that the word 'application' is not confused with 'practical application' in prong two and include examples or discussion on how claim interpretation affects integration determinations in Step 2A Prong Two.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility Step 1: Statutory Categories (Four Categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify whether a claim falls within the statutory categories of patentable subject matter (e.g., process, machine, manufacture, composition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No substantive change noted, but keep section updated and consistent with rest of eligibility guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility Step 2: Whether a Claim Is Directed To A Judicial Exception (Step 2A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the claim 'recites' a judicial exception and whether any recited judicial exception is integrated into a practical application (two prongs of Step 2A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add discussion of Revised Step 2A: (1) whether the claim recites a judicial exception; and (2) whether a recited judicial exception is integrated into a practical application. Remove language equating 'recited' and 'directed to' and require examiners to 'slot' abstract ideas into a single abstract idea grouping per the proposed guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial Exceptions — identification and terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and identify judicial exceptions (abstract ideas, laws of nature, natural phenomena, products of nature) when making eligibility determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update terminology and examples; consider removing some older labels (e.g., 'mental processes' and 'mathematical algorithms' as umbrella terms) to match the three groupings used in the proposed guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2A Prong One — Recitation of a Judicial Exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether a claim recites (explicitly or inherently includes) a judicial exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep first and second paragraph discussions of 'recited' material; delete text superseded by new approach to identifying abstract ideas; remove any language that equates 'recited' with 'directed to.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2A Prong Two — Integration into a Practical Application
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether a recited judicial exception is integrated into a practical application such that the claim is not 'directed to' the exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add an 'Integration' section incorporating proposed guidance; include how particular claim limitations (e.g., machine, transformation, field of use) may or may not integrate an exception, and provide case examples and explanations of the new consideration addressing integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract Ideas — groupings and terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe abstract ideas using the proposed guidance groupings: mathematical concepts, certain methods of organizing human activity, and mental processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modify discussion to adopt these groupings, remove reliance on comparing claimed concepts to previously-identified court examples, and revise examples/hypotheticals to explain that abstract-idea exception includes these groupings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of Claims Not Directed To Abstract Ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and document examples of claims that are not directed to abstract ideas, including claims that improve computer functionality or other technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate into the larger 'Integration' section; cite appropriate parts of 2106.05 for considerations; update case examples (including cases decided after Aug 2017) and explain how those examples integrate the abstract idea into a practical application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Directed To Improvements In Computer Functionality Or Other Technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that claims which improve computer functionality or other technology are not abstract ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revise discussion to clarify difference between conventionality vis-à-vis prior art (used in improvements consideration) and WURC consideration; examiners should continue to give full weight to improvements in Step 2A while not treating WURC analysis as part of Step 2A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of Concepts The Courts Have Identified As Abstract Ideas — categorical breakdown
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorize court-identified abstract ideas into: (I) Fundamental Economic Practices, (II) Certain Methods of Organizing Human Activity, (III) An Idea 'Of Itself', (IV) Mathematical Relationships/Formulas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revise and align section breakdown to match proposed guidance definitions; combine/reorganize sections A-C where appropriate and delete irrelevant sections; add guidance on TC director approval when claims do not fall within enumerated categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental Economic Practices and Other Subcategories
rubrics_metrics.description: Map examples like financial hedging, insurance, and other economic concepts into the 'Certain methods of organizing human activity' grouping as relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align explanations to the proposed guidance: include commercial/legal interactions, managing relationships, advertising/marketing/sales activities under the 'Certain methods of organizing human activity' heading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical Concepts (as abstract ideas)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define mathematical concepts to include mathematical relationships, formulas (equations), and calculations (e.g., multiplying or adding numbers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revise case cites and remove older 'algorithms' discussion; use terminology consistent with proposed guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mental Processes (as abstract ideas)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define mental processes as concepts performed in the human mind (including observation, evaluation, judgment, or opinion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine related sections and align discussion to the proposed guidance's explanation of this grouping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laws of Nature, Natural Phenomena & Products of Nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Address claims that potentially recite laws of nature, natural phenomena, or products of nature and when such claims can be rendered eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add discussion (including from relevant memoranda) about how treatment steps can render a claim reciting a law of nature eligible in Step 2A (i.e., not directed to a law of nature) when appropriately integrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Markedly Different Characteristics Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the 'markedly different characteristics' test where applicable in product/nature analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No change indicated to this section — continue application consistent with existing MPEP text and case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility Step 2B — Whether A Claim Amounts To Significantly More
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether claimed additional elements, individually and in combination, add an 'inventive concept' (i.e., amount to 'significantly more' than a judicial exception).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revise text to indicate how considerations are evaluated in both Step 2A Prong Two (integration) and Step 2B (significantly more), clarify overlap with WURC consideration (WURC evaluated only in 2B), and modify case exemplar discussions to address both integration and significantly more.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search For An Inventive Concept
rubrics_metrics.description: When performing Step 2B, search for an inventive concept in the additional claim elements beyond the judicial exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain when analysis from 2A may carry over to 2B and when it must be re-evaluated; clarify that WURC is an evidentiary, factual consideration to be evaluated only in 2B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-Understood, Routine, Conventional Activity (WURC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether additional claim elements are well-understood, routine, and conventional — a consideration relevant to Step 2B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add indication that WURC is evaluated only in 2B; remove language suggesting a WURC finding need not be supported. Add section addressing that WURC requires a factual determination and how examiners can support this determination (Berkheimer-related guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Particular Machine Limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether a 'particular machine' limitation integrates a judicial exception into the claim or provides significantly more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make language generic to apply to both 2A (integration) and 2B (significantly more); remove references that treat this solely as a 2B consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particular Transformation Limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether a particular transformation integrates the exception or amounts to significantly more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make language generic to apply to both 2A and 2B and remove references that limit discussion to 2B considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvements vs. WURC Distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between 'improvements to technology' (evaluated with respect to prior art) and WURC (evaluated as well-understood, routine, conventional activity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revise MPEP to distinguish (i) conventionality vs. prior art in the improvements consideration and (ii) WURC in Step 2B, so examiners continue to give full weight to improvements in revised Step 2A while not conflating with WURC analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Meaningful Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether other meaningful claim limitations integrate the exception or provide significantly more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make language generic to apply to both Step 2A Prong Two (integration) and Step 2B (significantly more).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere Instructions To Apply An Exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify when claim language merely instructs to apply an exception and does not integrate it into a practical application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the discussion generic to both 2A and 2B: mere 'apply it' instructions are relevant to integration and to whether something provides significantly more.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insignificant Extra-Solution Activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect when claim elements are insignificant extra-solution activity that do not integrate an exception nor add significantly more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make language generic to apply to both 2A and 2B and revise examples and references (e.g., to Flook) accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field Of Use And Technological Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate field of use or technological-environment limitations for whether they integrate an exception or add an inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify that a field-of-use limitation often fails to integrate a judicial exception into the claim as a whole and thus cannot 'practically apply' the exception in Step 2A Prong Two or add an inventive concept in Step 2B; modify related discussion to be consistent with proposed guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlined Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply streamlined analysis procedures (2106.06 et seq.) where appropriate for straightforward eligibility determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No change indicated for streamlined analysis section; ensure alignment with revised Step 2A/2B language where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulating A Rejection For Lack Of Subject Matter Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: When making a §101 rejection, identify/explain the judicial exception recited in the claim (Step 2A) and explain why additional claim elements do not result in the claim as a whole amounting to significantly more (Step 2B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align with proposed guidance: require examiners to identify the grouping of subject matter (mathematical concepts, certain methods of organizing human activity, mental processes), remove discussion comparing claimed concepts to previously identified court examples, modify and add examples, and add a section detailing the requirement to explain why the judicial exception is not integrated into a practical application. Revise discussion of the 1st and 2nd steps of the test and require clear explanatory language in rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary Requirements And Examiner's Burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the examiner's burden to provide factual support when making a §101 rejection (including WURC findings) and how to document that support in the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove/replace prior Berkheimer text as needed and add a memorandum-style section explaining how examiners must support rejections factually and how to structure the supporting evidence in the file history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluating Applicant's Response (Challenges to Official Notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how to evaluate and respond to applicant arguments challenging examiner reliance on Official Notice or other factual assertions in §101 rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revise MPEP to address evaluation of challenges to Official Notice and include memorandum guidance on how to evaluate and respond to applicant arguments; update procedures for considering applicant evidence and rebuttals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarifying The Record
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the prosecution record is clear and includes necessary explanations when making or responding to §101 rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No change indicated; continue existing practices for clarifying and documenting the record in applicant responses and examiner actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraphs — update and additions
rubrics_metrics.description: Update the library of form paragraphs used for §101 rejections and responses to reflect revised analysis (add new paragraphs and remove or revise outdated ones).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add new form paragraphs (e.g., 7.05.016, 7.05.017, 7.05.018) to reflect that additional elements are reviewed in both steps; remove FP 7.05.015 and revise related form-paragraph guidance to require explanation of why the judicial exception is not integrated into a practical application.
